subject: general
question: P and Q together can fill a cistern with water in 14 hours. If P alone can fill the cistern with water in 28 hours, then in how many hours will Q alone fill one-fourth of the same cistern with water?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(14, 28) = 28 units.

Efficiency: (P + Q) = 2 units/hour, P = 1 unit/hour.

Efficiency of Q = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour.

Time for Q to fill 1/4 of the cistern = (28 × 1/4) ÷ 1 = 7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P and Q together = 14 hours

Time taken by P alone = 28 hours

**Method Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Q = Efficiency of (P + Q) − Efficiency of P

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Total capacity of the cistern = 28 units

⇒ One-fourth of the capacity = 28 × (1/4) = 7 units

⇒ Time taken by Q to fill one-fourth of the cistern = 7 ÷ 1 = 7 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the cistern, so its efficiency is positive (+). An outlet pipe empties the cistern, so its efficiency is taken as negative (−).

Fraction of Work

If a person can complete a work in X days, then the time required to complete a fraction (a/b) of the work is (X × a/b) days.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple pipes operate together, their combined rate is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.
